prompts.text: Which part of our shared life reflects a choice we have never discussed?
Tell me about a moment you understood the weight of a responsibility I carry.
What would help us make important decisions without one person becoming the default authority?
Our relationship needs room for disappointment which is not a threat to staying together. How do we create it?
A goal important to one of us requires sacrifices from both. What should we agree before proceeding?
Reconsider a habit which saves time or a habit which protects emotional comfort?
What would you like me to understand about how your parents handled money?
We sometimes thank each other for visible tasks and miss the planning behind them. What planning should I recognise?
Describe a time you felt we were on the same side despite wanting different outcomes.
What do you want our shared future to leave room for in your individual life?
A work opportunity benefits one person while disrupting both routines. What would fair consideration involve?
Which form of reassurance have we made too dependent on perfect wording?
A shared decision deserves revisiting when its cost becomes clearer. Which decision would benefit from another look?
Tell me about a journey we took which changed how you saw us as a couple.
Protect a familiar way of spending time or create a ritual suited to our current responsibilities?
What does feeling consulted involve before a plan reaches its final stage?
Our different reactions to uncertainty sometimes hide different responsibilities. What responsibility shapes your reaction?
One of us needs practical relief while the other offers affection. How could we translate the need clearly?
Which expectation about partnership have we accepted mainly because other people call it normal?
Describe a time our relationship made it easier for you to act on a personal value.
What would make a conversation about unequal effort feel fair to you?
Our private way of repairing conflict matters more than appearing harmonious to others. What should remain private?
A family expectation conflicts with something we agreed together. What would we need to discuss before responding?
Review how we make plans or how we decide a plan needs changing?
Which part of being dependable for me leaves you needing support elsewhere?
Tell me about a moment we handled vulnerability better than either expected.
How should we decide whose belongings have a place in a shared room?
What helps you feel I respect your judgement when I do not follow your advice?
One of us wants a purchase the other finds difficult to justify. What meanings should we explore before numbers?
A partnership needs permission to admit an agreed plan is no longer working. What makes that admission easier?
Which difference between us has become a source of balance rather than friction?
Hear what I need less of or what I want more space for?
Describe a moment when you noticed our relationship becoming more resilient.
What do you want me to understand before calling a task easy?
One person's flexibility sometimes becomes the foundation of everyone's plans. Where should we check for this in us?
We need to choose between comfort now and a longer-term benefit. What would help both views be heard?
Which part of our relationship has benefited from help or perspective outside it?
Neither of us should need to become distressed before a concern receives attention. What would early attention look like?
Tell me about a time you enjoyed watching me become absorbed in something I love.
Understand how we each recover after conflict or how we prevent the same conflict recurring?
What does a fair division of responsibility need to account for beyond available hours?
An old disagreement returns through a new practical issue. How would we identify the earlier concern?
We might agree about a goal and disagree about how much uncertainty to tolerate. Where does this show up?
Which small decision gives you a strong sense of belonging in our shared life?
Describe a time I helped you protect a boundary with somebody outside our relationship.
Being partners does not remove the value of asking before offering an opinion. Which subjects deserve a check-in?
If one of us needs care during an illness, which preferences should the other know before making arrangements?
Set aside uninterrupted time or remove a recurring source of interruption?
One of us wants company while completing chores; the other wants quiet. What should we understand about each need?
A partner's competence sometimes hides the effort required to remain competent. Which effort deserves rest?
Tell me about a time you felt I valued your limits as well as your generosity.
What would help us discuss the possibility of parenthood without treating uncertainty as a hidden answer?
Shared plans should reflect both people's ambitions, including the quieter ambition. What ambition needs a clearer place?
A change in income alters what each person contributes. What should stay equal even if amounts differ?
Revisit what we mean by stability or what we mean by progress?
What does moving somewhere new represent to each of us beyond a change of address?
Describe a moment you felt I understood why an ordinary decision mattered emotionally.
We sometimes solve a practical issue while leaving an emotional question unanswered. What question should we notice?
Which part of your relationship with your body would you like me to approach more thoughtfully?
Someone offers us advice based on a relationship very different from ours. How would we assess its fit?
Which holiday from your childhood would you like me to understand before we plan our own?
What would make your personal downtime feel genuinely protected in our relationship?
Plan how to share a demanding week or agree how to recognise when the plan becomes too much?
Describe a time we were good company for each other without doing anything memorable.
The person who remembers a deadline often becomes responsible for it. Which reminders should belong to both of us?
A commitment one of us made alone affects a shared weekend. What would a fair conversation include?
How should we handle a situation where one of our friends confides something about the other?
A practical favour should not silently purchase decision-making power. How do we keep help free from control?
What helps you tell me a familiar form of comfort does not fit today?
Describe an occasion when we respected each other's different grieving or recovery pace.
Understand the meaning of a difficult memory or discuss what it affects in our present routines?
A goal we once shared matters less to one person now. How would we explore the change without accusing them of giving up?
We sometimes use the same word for different needs. What does 'support' mean in a difficult week for you?
What would help you feel comfortable attending something alone when I do not want to go?
Commitment includes maintaining honest conversations about consent and comfort. Which everyday assumption should we check?
Tell me about a time our different strengths helped without making either person feel less capable.
What does a closed door mean to each of us when we are at home?
Improve how we begin difficult conversations or how we return after a pause?
One of us wants to share a personal success publicly while the other values privacy around it. What should we clarify?
How would you like us to talk about an inheritance before assumptions grow around it?
Which outside relationship helps you bring a fuller version of yourself into ours?
A partner's change does not always signal dissatisfaction with the relationship. What helps us remain curious about change?
Describe a time you felt we protected each other's dignity during a disagreement.
Which demands of your work are hardest for me to understand from the outside?
One of us needs help but feels protective of how a task gets done. What would respectful assistance involve?
Share responsibility for a recurring task or alternate complete ownership of it?
What would make it easier to tell me you dislike a gift while appreciating the thought behind it?
Which wish have you described as impractical before letting me hear its meaning?
Describe a moment when meeting someone from my past helped you understand me differently.
Partners should be able to ask for help with the relationship without assigning all fault. What would make this safe?
What would a thoughtful conversation about our different social needs include?
An unexpected expense forces us to change a plan important to one person. What should we acknowledge before adjusting it?
Understand how we each recognise exhaustion or how we ask for relief?
How should we decide what happens to photographs and messages from before our relationship?
Describe a time we let a disappointing day remain disappointing without blaming each other.
Which expectations about hospitality did we each bring into our relationship?
A relationship should leave room for changing a preference without defending every earlier choice. What has changed for you?
We receive conflicting invitations from people important to each of us. What would a fair decision-making process look like?
What would you want me to know about your wishes if you were unable to speak for yourself?
Discuss how we welcome overnight guests or how we protect time to ourselves afterwards?
Tell me about a time I trusted your judgement before I understood your reasoning.
What do our separate morning routines reveal about how we each prepare to face a day?
Which part of my care feels different from what you learnt to expect earlier in life?
A partner needs room to disappoint an expectation which was never agreed. What expectation should we examine?
One of us wants advice about a problem involving the other's family. How could we make the conversation fair?
How do you want me to respond if someone comments on your appearance in front of us?
Name what we have become better at or acknowledge what still takes effort?
Describe a time one of us changed a plan because we understood the other's emotional cost.
Which experiences have shaped what borrowing or lending money means to you?
Which part of our relationship becomes clearer when we spend time apart?
Mutual respect includes noticing when humour no longer feels mutual. What would make it easy to say so?
A person outside the relationship treats one of us disrespectfully at a gathering. What support would the affected person want?
What does returning home feel like to you after you have spent time with your family?
Understand a personal value I hold quietly or explain one of yours which shapes many small decisions?
Tell me about a time a practical decision revealed how much we trusted each other.
A partner's wish for predictability and another's wish for novelty both have meanings. What meanings matter to us?
Which possessions would you want us to photograph before parting with them?
We need not agree that a feeling is reasonable before responding with care. What makes this difficult sometimes?
If we chose to care for an animal, which responsibilities should we discuss before falling in love with one?
Make space for an individual ambition this year or reassess the pace of a shared ambition?
Describe a time you felt I protected your confidence without hiding a difficult truth.
What would help us notice when a compromise costs the same person more repeatedly?
Which of our conversations would you like us to have while walking rather than sitting face to face?
Taking responsibility for a mistake should not require agreeing with every interpretation of it. How would we separate these?
One of us wants to return to a difficult conversation sooner than the other. What would make a pause trustworthy?
What would make it easier to tell me a familiar scent, sound or touch has become uncomfortable?
Understand how the other person experiences a responsibility or trade it briefly to learn through doing?
Tell me about a time you felt we respected an important difference without trying to solve it.
One person's calm might look like indifference to another. How would you like us to check meanings?
What helps you tell me you want closeness without needing to create a problem first?
How do you want us to handle a birthday when the person celebrating has had a difficult year?
We reach an important milestone and feel differently about it. How could both emotional responses belong?
Describe a time we were guests somewhere and learnt something about our own way of living.
Which part of sharing a bed or sleeping space is hardest to explain without sounding unromantic?
Ask for a change to the plan or ask for a change to how we make plans?
What should happen when a promised surprise clashes with something the other person needs to plan?
What have you learnt about my relationship with food which you wish you had understood earlier?
A difficult week leaves both of us less generous than usual. What would protect respect while we recover?
What do you want us to understand about how stress changes your way of speaking?
Tell me about a time we looked after something together and felt proud of its progress.
Recognise the care we already give or identify care neither of us has known how to ask for?
We sometimes hold a partner to a standard we silently exempt ourselves from. Which standard deserves a fair review?
How would you like us to respond if a medical professional addresses only one of us?
A relationship needs space for personal growth which has no immediate explanation. What kind of patience does this require?
Someone assumes one of us has the final say in our relationship. What would you want our response to express?
Describe a time you noticed I had taken something you said seriously through a later action.
Which places in our neighbourhood have become part of our relationship story?
Name a shared strength we rely on or a vulnerability we should care for more deliberately?
Partners sometimes ask for a solution when they first need someone to witness a difficulty. How do we signal the difference?
What does a fair approach to our different tolerances for financial risk involve?
Love should not make either person the permanent translator of every emotional need. What could we both learn to say directly?
One of us accepts extra work assuming the other will absorb its effects. What should have been discussed first?
Tell me about a time you heard me speak about you when I did not realise you were listening.
Which memory helps you trust we have learnt from an earlier difficulty?
Discuss what security means in daily life or what freedom means within commitment?
A person might enjoy being needed while needing relief from responsibility. How would we talk about both honestly?
How should we navigate a religious or spiritual practice one of us values and the other does not share?
We disagree about giving help to somebody outside the relationship. What commitments and limits should we consider together?
What helps you feel your interests deserve time even when they do not produce practical benefits?
Which habit from living alone do you miss, and what part of it would you like back?
Keep a difficult discussion between us or ask an agreed, trusted person to help us understand it?
Our ways of showing commitment may have changed since the beginning. What current behaviour carries that meaning?
What would help us notice when alcohol or another coping habit is changing how we relate?
What are you comfortable with me sharing about your life in a group chat?
A shared plan succeeds but leaves one of us feeling unseen. What would be worth hearing after the celebration?
Tell me about a time I made room for your feelings about something I experienced differently.
How do you want us to respond if one person enjoys a shared hobby more seriously than the other?
Discuss what an ideal day allows us to do or what it allows us to stop carrying?
Which room or corner would you like to feel more like a refuge, and why?
Our relationship should leave room for saying 'I need help learning how to do this.' What needs learning now?
An opportunity requires one of us to move temporarily. What emotional questions belong beside the logistics?
What would you like me to understand about your relationship with your own name?
Describe a time you felt we shared responsibility for a conversation instead of waiting for one person to begin it.
Revisit an agreement made in a calmer season or make a temporary arrangement for the present one?
What happens emotionally for you when we are running late, and how should I respond?
How do you want us to handle invitations which include one of us and leave the other out?
Shared history should help us ask better questions rather than stop asking them. What question has matured for us?
What would a thoughtful conversation about supporting an ageing relative need to include for both of us?
Tell me about a time I respected a personal choice which made our shared life less convenient.
Which language or expression from your background carries a feeling you struggle to translate for me?
Understand what makes a decision feel safe or what makes it feel freely chosen?
How should we handle a shared digital account which one person wants to stop using?
We should be allowed to celebrate improvement without claiming every problem is solved. What improvement deserves recognition?
One of us is ready to discuss a future responsibility while the other feels overwhelmed. How would we agree on a next conversation?
What does having savings of your own mean to you emotionally?
Describe a moment when we made a difficult situation feel more humane for each other.
Ask what a partner wants to preserve or what they need permission to change?
Our relationship includes choices which outsiders never notice. Which private choice are you glad we made?
What would help us talk openly about feeling lonely while living together?
How would you like us to respond when a child asks us a difficult question about our relationship?
We discover a shared goal means different things emotionally to each of us. How would we compare those meanings?
Tell me about a time you noticed a quality in me which I did not recognise in myself.
Which form of mutual respect do you want us to practise more consistently?
Protect time for a personal concern or share it early enough for joint understanding?
What would you want us to discuss before either of us made a public announcement about our future?
Being a team should include making room for an individual answer. Where do we need this most?
A plan important to both of us is no longer possible. What would we need to acknowledge before choosing a replacement?
Describe a time you felt our commitment made room for your uncertainty rather than removing it.
Which experience would you prefer us to leave undocumented so we stay present together?
What have we learnt about offering comfort when neither of us knows what happens next?
